summary: Rollback strategy for interleaved quantization profile + prefix/KV cache updates causing tail latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLens reported a production tail-latency regression after a combined rollout that changed the quantization profile and enabled aggressive prefix/KV cache prefetching for several dedicated pools. The change was deployed as a single staged rollout targeting the dedicated us-east pools; after the rollout completed, a subset of requests began to show 2--5x tail latency increases and intermittent 502s for long streaming responses.

Impact:
- User-facing: slow responses and occasional failed streams for ~9% of requests in the affected pools.
- Business: impacts BrightLens' inference SLAs for their internal quota-bearing tenant.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool: brightlens-prod-us-east (NVIDIA H100, 8 gpus per node)
- Serving runtime: 2026.02.2-build
- Config service snapshot: snap-2026-03-10-21:18

Steps to reproduce (observed on prod metrics):
1) Send a 2k token streaming request to the chat endpoint pinned to vicuna-13b-v1 for the brightlens tenant.
2) Observe initial streaming tokens, then a stall where latency for token N+1000 increases dramatically compared to baseline.
3) Check request logs and see 502 or incomplete stream in ~1 out of 12 failing traces.

Expected behavior:
- No substantial change in P95/P99 latency for streaming long-context requests after optimizer/profile rollout.
- No 502s introduced by optimizer changes.

Actual behavior:
- P95 increased from ~180ms to ~480ms; P99 up to ~1.8s on large-context streaming requests in affected pool.
- 502s appear tied to internal timeouts during KV-cache prefetch + quantized kernel path for certain shard placements.

Immediate ask:
Guidance for a safe rollback plan that avoids data loss (preserve warmed KV cache where possible), minimizes customer downtime, and provides verification steps. Customer specifically requests a recommended sequence because quant profile and KV-cache toggles were interleaved in one change set.
comments: 2026-03-11 09:05 - Ava Kim: Created ticket after first customer support call; assigned to Marcus for owned rollback plan.

2026-03-11 10:12 - Marcus Chen: Acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: quantization change introduced slower kernel for long sequences on some shards; combined with aggressive KV cache prefetch load caused sporadic routing backpressure and timeouts. Will assemble playbook and coordinate with SRE for controlled rollback.

2026-03-11 14:28 - SRE Oncall (Priya Singh): Confirmed transient pod restarts in brightlens-prod-us-east starting 2026-03-11T13:40Z. Noticed elevated kernel fusion stall counters on nodes hosting model shard group G-3. Pinning network I/O looked normal.

2026-03-12 08:00 - Marcus Chen: Drafted stepwise rollback (see investigation notes). Requested customer permission to perform staged rollback during off-peak window 2026-03-12 23:00-01:00 UTC. Customer approved.
2026-03-13 02:14 - Marcus Chen: Performed initial rollback of quant profile on 20% of the pool and adjusted traffic split. Observed immediate drop in P99 for those hosts. Continuing phased rollback.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Quantization profile changed kernel selection causing a slow path at long attention windows on certain devices (H100 firmware + selected GEMM kernel mismatch).
Hypothesis 2: KV cache prefetch aggressive setting increased memory pressure and concurrent IO which amplified kernel stalls, leading to internal timeouts in the streaming pipeline.
Metric evidence: Correlation between hosts where quant profile flip occurred and elevated 'attention_kernel_slow' counter. Hosts with both quant flip and prefetch enabled showed highest error rates.
Log excerpts: timeouts in stream-writer: "write timeout after 120s"; serving-runtime stack traces show stalled kernel invocation during decode loop for sequence positions > 1024.
A/B rollback sanity check: Reverting only quant on a small subset returned P99 to baseline; reverting only KV-cache prefetch reduced 502s but did not fully restore P99. Suggests interaction effect.
recommended_rollback_steps: 1) Take a config snapshot: config-service create-snapshot --pool brightlens-prod-us-east --tag pre-rollback-2026-03-13

2) Phase A - Quant profile soft rollback: use gradual traffic split to move 30% of traffic off new quant profile to previous profile for vicuna-13b-v1. Command: redwoodctl rollout traffic --pool brightlens-prod-us-east --model vicuna-13b-v1 --from-profile quant-new-2026-03-10 --to-profile quant-stable-2026-02-28 --percent 30 --wait 60s
3) Monitor P95/P99, kernel stall counters, and 5xx rate for 15 minutes. If P99 reduction observed, continue to 60% then 100% in 20m increments.

4) If quant rollback alone does not fully resolve 502s, Phase B - KV cache pref instead of full flush: disable aggressive prefix prefetch at pool level (toggle to conservative prefetch) to avoid flushing warmed caches: redwoodctl config set --pool brightlens-prod-us-east --kv-prefetch conservative

5) If disabling prefetch is insufficient, perform controlled KV cache eviction on a single node to ensure a clean warm path: redwoodctl node evict-kv --node <node-id> --pool brightlens-prod-us-east, then observe behavior for that node before wider action.
6) Avoid doing both full-quant rollback and full cache flush simultaneously. Prefer quant rollback first, then conservative prefetch toggle, then targeted node-level evictions if needed.

7) Post-rollback validation: run a standardized set of long-context streaming synthetic requests (provided in runbook) and confirm P95/P99 are within 10% of baseline for 30 minutes; inspect streaming completeness and absence of 502s.

8) After verification, create a postmortem runbook item and schedule a follow-up config change that separates quant profile changes from cache prefetch toggles in future rollouts (no interleaved changes).
resolution: Workaround applied: Gradual rollback of quant profile to stable for vicuna-13b completed at 2026-03-13T03:12Z. P99 on rolled hosts dropped back to baseline within 2 minutes.
Customer-facing outcome: BrightLens confirmed improved response latency and reduced failed streams during their peak across the affected pool segments.

Permanent fix path: Recommend splitting future optimizer rollouts into two distinct steps with canary windows: (A) quant/profile changes validated on isolated shards; (B) KV-prefetch changes applied after at least 24h stable telemetry. Engineering to add a preflight check for 'kernel_slow' counters before promoting quant profiles.
Follow-up: ENG-OPS action item created to add health-check gating in the config-service for combined optimizer changes. Scheduled change review with BrightLens on 2026-03-18.
follow_up_actions: ENG: Implement kernel-slow preflight check in config-service (owner: @marcus). Target ETA: 2026-03-20.
SRE: Add automated alert that fires when 'attention_kernel_slow' counter increases > 3x baseline in a pool for 10m (owner: @priya).
CS: Coordinate BrightLens verification window and sign-off (owner: @ava).
PM: Update rollout playbook to disallow interleaved optimizer and cache changes in the same config snapshot.
